## Why this exists

This fork (`einarhjorleifsson/icesDatras`) tracks
[ices-tools-prod/icesDatras](https://github.com/ices-tools-prod/icesDatras) closely --
as of writing, one commit ahead of upstream `master`. While using the package as a
dependency of another project ([obus](https://github.com/einarhjorleifsson/obus)),
several real, reproducible bugs surfaced. This article documents what was found, what
was fixed, why -- and, just as importantly, one thing that looked like a bug but wasn't.

Everything here lives on `einar_dev/integration` in this fork, not yet on `master` and
not yet proposed upstream. It's written up both as a personal reference and as a
starting point should it be worth raising with the people maintaining the upstream
repository.

## A three-way distinction that shaped what got "fixed" here

Not every wrong-looking result is fixable the same way:

- **Code bug** -- given the same values the DATRAS API already returns, a function's
  own logic produces a result that contradicts a clear, well-defined convention.
  Fixable permanently in this package's own R source.
- **Data bug** -- the values themselves, as submitted to DATRAS, are wrong or
  inconsistent regardless of what any client code does with them. Not fixable here at
  all.
- **Webserver/schema gap** -- ICES's own field-list webservice
  (`getDatrasFieldList()`) is missing or wrong, even though the underlying survey data
  is fine. Fixable here only as an interim, escapable patch -- the real fix belongs on
  ICES's server.

This distinction is what kept one investigation (below) from turning into an incorrect
"fix."

## Fixes

### 1. `-9` sentinel not fully scrubbed to `NA`

`applyDatrasTypeSchema()` coerced column types but never converted DATRAS's `-9`
missing-value sentinel to `NA`. `parseDatras()` already caught the *string* `"-9"`, but
not decimal forms like `"-9.0"` -- a valid representation DATRAS uses for missing float
fields. After `simplify()` converts such a string to numeric, the value becomes `-9`
and passed through unchanged.

```r
x <- data.frame(HaulDur = -9)
applyDatrasTypeSchema(x, record = "HH")$HaulDur
#> [1] -9      # before the fix -- should be NA
```

**Fix:** explicit `-9`/`-9L` scrubbing added to `applyDatrasTypeSchema()` for all
`int`/`decimal` columns, after type coercion.

### 2. Empty or unavailable results returned `FALSE`/`NULL` instead of a data frame

`getDATRAS()`, `getFlexFile()`, `getLTassessment()`, `getIndices()`, and
`getCatchWgt()` all had at least one path that returned a bare `FALSE` (an invalid
survey name, an unavailable year/quarter) or, for `getDATRAS()`, silently returned
`NULL` when an empty XML response collapsed via `do.call(rbind, .)`. Both break
idiomatic downstream code:

```r
out <- getDATRAS("HH", "NS-IBTS", years = 1800, quarters = 1)
nrow(out)
#> Error: argument is not a data frame
```

**Fix:** every such early exit now returns `data.frame()`. `getCatchWgt()` needed a
genuinely new guard -- it has no availability checks of its own, it inherits failure
from two internal `getDATRAS()` calls, and would otherwise hard-error on
column-dependent processing against an empty result.

### 3. `xsi:nil` XML attribute leaking into column names

DATRAS represents a missing field as a self-closing tag, e.g.
`<Age_6 xsi:nil="true" />`. `parseDatras()`'s name-extraction regex relied on a lazy
quantifier (`(.*?)`) that isn't reliably supported across regex engines, and captured
the whole `Age_6 xsi:nil="true"` as the column name instead of `Age_6`.

**Fix:** replaced with `([^ >]+)[^>]*`, which stops the capture at the first space or
`>` without relying on lazy-quantifier support. Verified live: all 16 `Age_0`-`Age_15`
columns from a real `getIndices()` call now come back with clean names.

### 4. Literal text `"NA"` surviving as a real, non-missing value

A deeper, separate bug in the same area: the self-closing-tag expansion in
`parseDatras()` produced the *literal text* `"NA"` as the field's content, not a true
`NA`. Two lines later, `-9` and `""` are explicitly normalised to `NA` -- but `"NA"`
was never included, and `is.na("NA")` is `FALSE`, so `simplify()`'s numeric-conversion
guard was fooled and left the whole column as `character`, holding the string `"NA"` in
every affected cell.

**Fix:** the tag expansion now produces empty content rather than the literal text
`"NA"`, so the existing `x[x == ""] <- NA` normalisation catches it -- for every column
type, not just numeric ones. This was a real gap beyond `Age_*`: declared-character
columns got zero scrubbing either.

### 5. Field-list webserver gaps (interim patches, not code bugs)

Two corrections to `getDatrasFieldList()`'s existing hot-fix block, both examples of
the third category above:

- **`aphia` naming** -- the hot-fix had invented `aphia` as the "new" name for
  `Valid_Aphia`. Cross-checked against ICES's own `getHLdataNewHeaders` endpoint (the
  one place ICES is actively rolling out new header names) -- it still calls this
  field `Valid_Aphia`, unchanged. Realigned to match ICES's actual direction rather
  than this repo's own invention.
- **CA `Age` gap** -- `getDATRAS("CA", ...)` returns a column literally named `Age`,
  matching neither the field list's `IndividualAge` (new) nor `AgeRings` (old) -- even
  with `new_names = FALSE`, confirming the raw server response itself uses `Age`.
  Corrected the field list's `FieldNameOld` accordingly, the same pattern already used
  for three analogous LT corrections.

## Investigated, not fixed: `getCatchWgt()` and `DataType == "C"`

The most interesting negative result. `getCatchWgt()` never applies a
`HaulDuration/60` scaling for `DataType == "C"` hauls -- initial evidence (2020 data)
showed catch weights inflated by exactly that factor on affected hauls. This looked
like a clean code bug.

But `R/zzz.R`'s own package-startup message already warns: *"there are known issues
with the way CatCatchWgt has been reported until 2023."* That's ICES's own disclaimer,
and it lines up: checking real NS-IBTS 2024 Q1 data, the median catch-per-minute-towed
for `DataType == "C"` hauls is **~0.97x** the `DataType == "R"` rate -- not ~60x.
Post-2023 submissions are already correctly per-haul.

Applying the "obvious" fix now would have *broken* current and future data while only
helping historical records. Conclusion: a data bug, time-bounded and already resolved,
not a `getCatchWgt()` code bug. No change made.

## What's next

Two of the fixes above map directly onto an issue already filed upstream by the same
author: [#48](https://github.com/ices-tools-prod/icesDatras/issues/48) (fixes 3 and 4).
[#47](https://github.com/ices-tools-prod/icesDatras/issues/47) is adjacent to the
field-list gaps in fix 5. Whether/when to send any of this as pull requests to
`ices-tools-prod/icesDatras` is a separate, unhurried decision.
